products.name: Elai.io
products.note: AI avatar video; text-to-video; multilingual; enterprise training; consent

reading.body:
Elai is a text-to-video platform that generates training and presentation videos using AI avatars and speech synthesis, positioning itself in the enterprise training market rather than content creation at scale.

The product sits downstream of substantial compute requirements. Text-to-video generation and avatar synthesis demand real-time or near-real-time inference, which means Elai's operations depend on access to GPUs or specialized inference hardware. The emphasis on enterprise training use cases suggests the company targets customers with predictable, recurring demand for video content, where the cost per video can be amortized across many employees and repeated uses. This is a different scaling pattern than consumer-facing video generation, which would face vastly larger inference loads.

The data does not cover Elai's infrastructure ownership, cloud provider relationships, or whether the platform is self-hosted or SaaS-delivered. It does not specify which models power the text-to-video capability, the latency of video generation, or the compute cost per output. The note that Panopto powers the platform suggests partnership or integration rather than fully proprietary technology, but the nature of that relationship is not detailed here. Without operational metrics, it is unclear whether Elai's growth is currently constrained by compute availability, data center capacity, or market demand.

profile_text.body:
Elai.io is an AI video generator that the company describes as an AI training video generator, powered by Panopto. According to its site, it creates presentations using text to speech and AI avatars, and users can select from a cast of video presenters or create their own avatar. The company markets it as intuitive and aimed at producing high-quality video content, with free signup offered.

The product is also described as covering AI avatar video, text-to-video, multilingual output, enterprise training, and consent. No litigation, patent, or securities filings are recorded for the company.
